This rise is attributed to vaccine hesitancy, influenced by political factors, and widespread hypovitaminosis D, which compromises innate immunity. Low levels of vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) are associated with heightened susceptibility to respiratory infections, particularly as autumn humidity decreases, leading to mucosal dryness that facilitates viral entry. The article highlights various respiratory viruses, including influenza A (H1N1, H3N2), B, parainfluenza, rhinovirus, adenovirus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and coronaviruses, including MERS-CoV. While vaccines are available for influenza and RSV, most respiratory viruses lack effective vaccines, emphasizing the urgent need for additional preventive strategies and medically supervised vitamin D supplementation to bolster immunity and reduce infection rates.
